partners.mechanism_chain: AP3B1 (HGNC:543) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosome-related organelle dysfunction (HP:0030054); Lysosome-related organelle dysfunction (HP:0030054) —LEADS_TO→ Albinism (HP:0001053); TP53 (HGNC:11998) —DISRUPTS→ Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049); Cell cycle regulation (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatocellular carcinoma (MONDO:0007256); TP53 (HGNC:11998) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatocellular carcinoma (MONDO:0007256). Loss-of-function mutations in AP3B1 (Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome 2) lead to lysosome-related organelle dysfunction and albinism. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TP53, a gene causally linked to hepatocellular carcinoma, disrupt cell cycle regulation. The convergence lies in the shared role of TP53 in maintaining genomic stability and preventing tumorigenesis, where its dysfunction in HCC can be exacerbated by cellular stress pathways that might also be subtly affected by broader cellular dysregulation stemming from HPS2.
